title: Example 17-13: Partial Emphasis Using Mathematical Symbols

illustrates.quote: Mathematical Symbols. Spellers often use mathematical symbols to teach word formation. a. Transcribe all text in word formation “equations” in uncontracted braille. b. If the result of the equation is a complete word, add the contracted form of the word at the end of the equation, enclosed in transcriber’s note indicators. Ignore any print emphasis.

print.notes: A cell-5 heading, then two word-formation equations with partial bold emphasis on the suffixes ('ment', 'ful') in both the equation and its result.
print.printFeatures: Bold on the suffix portion only, in both terms of each equation.

braille.notes: Byte-identical between A and B; matches independent re-extraction exactly.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille and rule id unchanged. Print's own partial bold on the suffix is NOT re-encoded here: even if marked, Emboss silently drops all typeform from an uncontracted run (F-210), so a bold sub-run and a plain one produce byte-identical output — omitting the bold marking changes nothing observable. The contracted-form annotation at the end of each equation is written here in ordinary parentheses because Emboss has no inline TN segment (F-211, 17.13.1b) — the given braille wraps it in `@.<...@.>`; expect mismatch there.
